And he repeated this evaluation in a letter to Claire Clairmont dated three days later: ‘I have
lately been composing a poem on Keats: it is better than any thing that I have yet written, &
worthy both of him & of me’ (L ii 296). S. was more self-deprecating in sending the poem
to Byron — ‘I fear it is worth little’ (L ii 309) — and Byron himself made no response. S.’s
concern for the critical fate of Adonais is underlined by his continuing interest in revisions
for a possible London edition, but after receiving no news of the poem from Ollier for several
months he wrote on 11 November 1821 ‘I am especially curious to hear the fate of Adonais.
